Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (博山無異大師語錄集要). The explicit “Shaolin master said” frame introduces Bodhidharma as quoted utterer; Wuyi Yuanlai is the quoter.

Occurrences.Kwic: 外息諸緣，內心無喘，心如牆壁，可以入道。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (吹萬禪師語錄). Chuiwan Guangzhen reproduces the established Bodhidharma formula in an authored teaching; Bodhidharma is the quoted utterer.

Senses.Explanation: The mind like a wall is a quoted formula that joins stopping external involvements and inner agitation with entering the Way. All four stored witnesses quote substantially the same formula: outwardly cease involvements, inwardly let the mind have no panting or agitation, and make the mind like a wall so that entry into the Way is possible. The evidence supports wall-like steadiness as a mental comparison. The separate saying “going is also unmoving” is not stored here, so this entry does not use it as proof or turn the formula into an unsupported historical claim about Bodhidharma’s physical posture.
